title: Smile and Room
premise: Marguerite Oyelaran takes a teaching post at Hollowmere Primary, where a class of children vanished decades ago and the surviving staff survive by strict ritual: lights on, doors counted, never singing the school song's final verse. When her bedroom mirror begins lagging one second behind reality, she realizes the missing class is trying to return through reflections—and that her own students are being chosen to replace them. To save them, Marguerite must learn the song's last verse from the ghost-children themselves without ever singing along, a bargain that demands she surrender her own reflection in their place. In the end she trades her mirrored self for the children's freedom, becoming the school's new unseen caretaker: present in every room, visible in no glass.
about_author: Gideon Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent eleven years in shuttered district schools before turning to horror. They write at night with every mirror in the house turned to face the wall.

chapters.title: The Counting of Doors
chapters.summary: Marguerite arrives at Hollowmere Primary and is handed an odd orientation packet: keep lights on, count doors twice daily, never sing past the second verse. Veteran teacher Mr. Ansel demonstrates the rituals without explanation. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity masked as professional composure.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Empty Seats
chapters.summary: Marguerite discovers her classroom roster lists thirty-two students but only six attend; the other twenty-six desks bear faded name cards from 1974. The custodian warns her not to remove the cards. At night she hears faint humming from the empty room. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: dread taking root beneath duty.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: Her bathroom mirror reflects her raising a hand a full second after she does it. Testing other mirrors, she finds the lag everywhere—and once, a small extra figure standing behind her reflection. She begins keeping a log. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: rational mind fracturing against evidence.

chapters.title: What Ansel Knows
chapters.summary: Marguerite confronts Ansel, who confesses the 1974 class sang the song's final verse during an assembly and was taken into the glass; staff have kept the rituals since to stay invisible to whatever took them. He begs her to stop investigating. POV: alternating Marguerite/Ansel. Emotional beat: loyalty to colleagues versus hunger for truth.

chapters.title: The Chosen Roster
chapters.summary: A seventh student appears—quiet Tamsin, whose name card matches one of the vanished. Her reflection moves independently, practicing the forbidden verse. Marguerite realizes the dead class is selecting replacements, one child per term. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: protective fury; the price of survival is no longer hers alone.

chapters.title: Verse by Verse
chapters.summary: Marguerite researches the school song in the archive, finding the final verse torn from every copy except one hidden in the piano bench. The lyrics are a summons written as a lullaby. That night all mirrors show the 1974 classroom, children mouthing the words. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: horrified fascination tipping toward complicity.

chapters.title: Doors Miscounted
chapters.summary: Marguerite misses the evening door count during a storm; by morning two more students' reflections are gone, and Tamsin has begun fading in photographs. Ansel tries to burn the last lyric sheet and is pulled into his own hallway mirror. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: guilt—the rules were protection, and she broke their spirit.

chapters.title: The Glass Assembly
chapters.summary: Following the lagging reflections, Marguerite steps through the auditorium mirror into the frozen 1974 assembly, where the vanished class waits mid-song. Their leader, a girl named Odile, explains the bargain: teach us the verse's true ending, unbroken for fifty years, and we can leave—but someone must remain. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; justice outside any law.

chapters.title: Without Singing Along
chapters.summary: In the real school, Marguerite gathers her living students and teaches them the final verse as pure recitation—words without melody, breath without song—as the mirrors shiver and the dead class leans close, hungry for voices to join. Tamsin nearly sings; Marguerite covers the child's mouth with her own hand. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: white-knuckle tenderness under siege.

chapters.title: The Last Verse, Sung Once
chapters.summary: At dawn the dead class begins the song themselves, and only a voice completing the verse inside the glass can seal the door. Marguerite enters the mirror and sings the ending alone, freeing the twenty-six and closing the way behind her. The children wake whole; the school finds only her lesson plans, neatly finished. POV: shifting to Tamsin. Emotional beat: grief braided with release—survival purchased, and paid in full.
